plan_a_advantages: Includes a hill workout to build climbing strength and power, a key component of trail running.
Features a longer run to improve endurance and trail-specific durability.
Incorporates a threshold intensity hill session, which is more effective for improving speed than solely easy runs.
plan_b_advantages: May be suitable for a complete beginner or someone returning from injury due to its lower overall volume and intensity.
The consistent easy runs could be beneficial for improving running economy if the athlete is currently very fatigued.
reasoning: Plan A is the better choice for an athlete aiming to become a faster trail runner. While both plans incorporate rest days, Plan A includes a dedicated hill workout and a longer run, both crucial for trail running performance. The hill workout specifically targets climbing strength and power, essential for tackling varied terrain, while the longer run builds endurance and trail-specific durability. Plan B focuses almost exclusively on easy runs, which, while important for base building, doesn't provide the stimulus needed to improve speed and efficiency on trails.
